steps.message:
Before I make this change: `userId` in `GET /users` is a public response field, and `README.md` states the consumers explicitly — the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export — and that "Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint."

Renaming it in place is a breaking change for all three consumers: any client reading `userId` gets `undefined` the moment this ships, with no error to signal it. iOS 3.2+ in particular can't be fixed by a deploy.

The one-line edit is `routes/users.js:6` — trivial to make, so I'm not stopping on difficulty, only on the contract.

questions.question: How should the userId -> user_id rename land, given the documented consumer contract?

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Add user_id alongside userId in GET /users. Non-breaking: existing consumers keep working while clients migrate; userId gets removed later once all three consumers are off it.

options.label: Rename in place anyway
options.description: Replace userId with user_id in GET /users now. Breaks the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export until each is updated. Choose this if you have already confirmed consumers are ready.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Follow the README process: leave GET /users unchanged and expose the snake_case shape on a new version (e.g. /v2/users). Largest change; more than the one-line edit you asked for.
